name: Benzydamine

overview.mechanism: Locally used anti-inflammatory treatment evaluated as an oral rinse for radiation-associated mucosal injury; rinse evidence does not define effects of swallowed or other topical formulations [[BENZ-RT]].
uses: Prevention of radiation-associated oral mucositis studied in selected head-and-neck cancer settings; verify local formulation-specific indications [[BENZ-RT]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Randomized double-blind trial; conventional-radiotherapy comparison included 69 benzydamine and 76 placebo recipients.
rows.findings: Through conventional RT up to 50 Gy, erythema/ulceration fell by about 30%; over 33% versus 18% remained ulcer-free. Benefit was not demonstrated in the small accelerated-radiotherapy subgroup.
rows.limitations: Regimen-specific supportive oncology evidence; does not establish prevention of every mucositis cause or extrapolation to sprays, lozenges or systemic use.

rows.design: Retrospective 724 reported ingestions of vaginal irrigation products.
rows.intervention: Nonoral products ingested accidentally, usually after being mistaken for an oral preparation.
rows.findings: Reported toxicity included gastrointestinal and neurological manifestations; hallucinations occurred and one child had convulsions.
rows.limitations: Selected poison-center reports, not incidence during correctly used oral rinse treatment. Products and routes must remain distinct.

sources.citation: Benzydamine HCl for prophylaxis of radiation-induced oral mucositis: results from a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. PubMed PMID: 11550161.
Ingestions of benzydamine-containing vaginal preparations. PubMed PMID: 18608296.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive monograph, clinical evidence and safety limitations without unsupported dosing or inferred dialysis regimen.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

common: Adverse-event incidence in the radiotherapy-rinse trial was comparable to placebo; discontinuation due to adverse events occurred in 6% versus 5% [[BENZ-RT]].
serious: Ingestion of nonoral benzydamine preparations has caused neurological toxicity, including hallucinations and a reported childhood convulsion; this differs from correctly using a topical rinse [[BENZ-POISON]].

renal: The cited topical trial does not establish renal dose adjustment, dialysis use or safety of systemic exposure. Do not transfer systemic NSAID renal assumptions or swallowed-drug regimens to a topical product without product-specific evidence [[BENZ-RT]].
